title: Interface Errors: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: The link is up. But everything is slow. The interface counters can tell you why.

lines.t: The counters will tell you why

scenes.heading: The parcel sorting office
scenes.narration: A sorting office has rules. Every parcel must be bigger than a shoebox and smaller than a suitcase. Too small is a runt, a broken fragment. Too big is a giant. If the seal doesn't match, that's a C R C error, usually a bad cable or noise. If two parcels crash on the belt late, that's a late collision, often a duplex mismatch. Watch which counter is growing, because it points straight at the cause.

scenes.heading: Where to look
scenes.narration: Start with show interfaces. Look at the input errors, C R C and collisions. And clear the counters, so you can watch what grows.

lines.note: Speed and duplex at a glance

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three habits to build. A growing C R C count means a physical problem, not a configuration one. Late collisions on a full duplex link point at a mismatch. And a few old errors don't matter if the number isn't climbing.

items.wrong: Any error count is a crisis
items.right: Only worry if it keeps growing

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva interface errors lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Check the counters whenever a link feels slow. C R C points at the cable, and late collisions point at duplex. Clear the counters, then watch what grows. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva interface errors lab.
